Definition: The number or value of customer orders received in a period.
The number of items sold in a period, counted in units rather than money.
Total order value divided by the number of orders.
Revenue divided by the number of users or subscribers in the period.
How much sales have gone up or down compared with an earlier period, shown as a percentage of that earlier period.
Sales from stores or outlets that were open in both periods being compared, so growth is not flattered by new openings.
The amount of sales a person, team or region is expected to reach in a period. Actual sales are measured against it.
How much of the sales target has been reached, shown as a percentage of the target.
The sales the business expects to make in a future period, usually built from pipeline, history and seasonality.
How close the sales forecast turned out to be to what was actually sold. A figure near 100% means the forecast was reliable.
The total value of open deals that could still be won. It is often compared with the target to see whether there is enough in the funnel.
Open deals counted at their chance of closing, for example a deal worth 100 with a 30% chance counts as 30. It is a more cautious view than the plain pipeline.
The number of potential sales that sales people are actively working on.
Leads that sales has checked and agreed are worth pursuing because they have a need, a budget and a decision maker.
Leads that marketing considers ready to pass to sales because they have shown enough interest, for example by downloading content or requesting a demo.

Also known as: Lead to Customer Rate; Lead to Opportunity Rate
Definition: The share of leads that move to the next stage, such as an opportunity or a paying customer.
How long it takes to make first contact after a lead arrives. Faster responses usually mean a better chance of winning the deal.
The average number of days from first contact with a prospect to a closed deal.

Also known as: Average Sale Value; Average Contract Value; ACV
Definition: The average value of the deals that were won in a period.
The number of deals that were signed in a period.
The number of deals that ended without a sale in a period.
The share of closed deals that were lost rather than won.

Also known as: Backlog of Orders; Open Orders Value
Definition: The value of orders taken but not yet delivered or invoiced. It shows how much work is already secured.
Orders received divided by sales invoiced in the same period. Above 1 means more orders are coming in than going out, which signals growth.

Also known as: Revenue per Sales Rep; Sales per Salesperson
Definition: The average sales made by each sales person in a period. It shows how productive the team is.
The share of sales people who reached their quota in the period.
The time a new sales person needs before reaching a normal level of sales.
How much sales are produced for the effort or cost put in, for example sales per rep or per sales call.
The number of calls the sales team made in a period. It measures activity, not results.
The number of meetings or demos that sales people arranged with prospects in a period.
The number of formal offers sent to customers in a period.

Also known as: Quote Conversion Rate; Quote Win Rate
Definition: The share of quotes sent that turned into orders.
The reduction from list price that was given on sales, as a percentage of list price. Deep discounts reduce profit.
Discounts given above what policy or approval rules allow. It is margin that was given away without a reason.
The share of the list price that the business actually collected after discounts and deductions.
The average price at which a product sold, found by dividing sales value by units sold.

Also known as: Margin per Order; Margin per Deal
Definition: The profit left on a sale after the direct cost of the goods or service has been taken off.
The share of customers who buy a different product or service from you on top of what they already have.
The share of customers who move to a more expensive product or add more of what they already buy.
How many add-on or related products are sold per main product, for example accessories per device sold.
The share of customers who buy again within a period. It shows loyalty and satisfaction.
How much of total sales comes from the biggest few customers. A high figure means the business depends on a small number of buyers.
Sales made to customers who bought for the first time in the period.

Also known as: Repeat Business Revenue; Installed Base Revenue
Definition: Sales made to customers who had already bought before the period started.
Sales split by geographic area, used to compare how regions are performing against each other.
Sales split by how they were made, such as direct, distributors, online or retail.
The portion of total market sales that the business holds. It shows how it is doing compared with competitors.
The share of deals won when a specific competitor was also bidding.
Variable pay earned by sales people for the sales they close, usually a percentage of the sale value.
How much new revenue is gained for each unit of sales and marketing spend.
The number of people who visited a store or site in a period. Together with the conversion rate it explains sales.

Also known as: Average Basket; Items per Basket; Units per Transaction
Definition: The average number of items in a customer's purchase.
The average money spent in one purchase, found by dividing sales by the number of transactions.

Also known as: Sales Density; Sales per Square Metre
Definition: The sales a store makes for each unit of selling floor space. It shows how well the space is being used.
